tasks.rejection_reason: The actual V0 supports hand-rolled raw flatbread from one unfinished batch, with both plain and filled continuations reasonable. The existing real Paul Hollywood beginner lesson teaches plain flatbread and enclosing arbitrary filling within raw dough, rolling it and pan-cooking it. That single useful guide remains sufficient under both source-supported continuations before V1. Requiring two separate dough disks, potato filling, the same formula or exact sealing details would add unsupported constraints merely to exclude a legitimate substitute. No actual V0 evidence supports introducing a pizza or another cooking system just to refute the general guide. The real later filling and sealing sequence does not supply a necessary selection correction for this task purpose.

observed_events.description: The wearer rolls an opaque round raw dough disk on the wooden board; another unrolled dough lump sits on a plate. The adjacent frying pan is empty. Full unmodified frames show no exposed filling bowl or completed filled flatbread. A covered pot is present but its contents and future use cannot be inferred.

The wearer places a coarse pale-yellow filling on raw dough, spreads it, places a second raw disk over it, and presses the entire rim closed. The adjacent frying pan is still empty. Two dough disks become one filled item before cooking; this is not an already cooked plain flatbread followed by an unrelated new item.

supported_claims.text: The initial released views show the wearer rolling one opaque raw dough disk on a wooden board; another dough piece lies on the plate, and the adjacent frying pan is empty. No exposed filling bowl or completed filled bread is visible; a covered pot does not establish its contents.

The later released views show a coarse pale filling spread on raw dough, another raw disk placed over it and the perimeter pressed closed. This is one unfinished filled flatbread, not a completed cooked plain item followed by another batch.
